title: Every D23 unit carries a requirements paragraph derived from its hidden tests
body:
The D23 task text gives the observable behaviour the hidden tests check (flags, exact output strings, exit codes, file shapes) without the implementation, SWE-bench Pro style.
Why: n100 judge labels 72/100 units N (tests assert exact strings/flags the text never gives; reasons in /mnt/storage/coding/krn/active/krn/.krn/runs/d23-comparison/n100/screen); both arms sit at ~10%. SWE-bench Pro: removing requirements+interface drops GPT-5 25.9% -> 8.4% (https://arxiv.org/html/2509.16941). Research: .krn/runs/lead/breakthrough/papers.md.
Outcome: evals/d23/ writes <pr>.requirements.txt from the hidden fail-to-pass tests with a model, never quoting test bodies or the merge diff; the judge (evals/d23/screen.ts) rescreens the 72 N units with interface+requirements.
Proof: rescreen prints D/P/N counts before 9/19/72 and after; target N <= 30 of 100.
Scope: evals/d23/, test/evals/, .krn/runs/d23-comparison/.
